title: Why Won’t Beijing Step On The Gas?
text:
Why Won’t Beijing Step On The Gas?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 9 Sep 2026

China today benefits from the cheapest cost of capital in the world, the cheapest cost of labor (at least when adjusted for productivity—see Unraveling China’s Productivity Paradox) and the cheapest cost of electricity. The country has also spent the past three decades building up domestic infrastructure. So much so that today China enjoys the world’s most complete rail network, an impressive system of highways, clean and efficient subways in almost all major cities, six of the top 10 largest ports in the world… On paper, the Chinese economy should thus be growing gangbusters. But obviously, this has not been the case; quite the contrary. In recent months, almost all Chinese macro data point releases, whether auto sales, retail sales, PMIs, housing starts… have underwhelmed.
